papers_read.title_as_printed: Tortuosity and discrete compactness biomarkers for machine learning-based classification of mild cognitive impairment (Torres Guzman, Pinzon Vivas, Barbara Morales; Biomed Signal Process Control 112 (2026) 108848)

Optimal transport- and kernel-based early detection of mild cognitive impairment patients based on magnetic resonance and positron emission tomography images (Liu et al., Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2022 14:4)

what_each_reports.P-125: Healthy controls vs MCI (37 vs 37, ADNI 1.5T T1 MRI), 8 amygdala features (volume, normalised volume, discrete compactness, tortuosity per hemisphere), 60/40 train/test split with 5-fold CV tuning. Abstract: test accuracy 82.14%, AUC 88.27-91.33%. Table 6: mean test accuracy RF 80.00 +/- 2.43, SVM 79.29, KNN 77.86, ANN 80.00; test AUC 85.71-90.31%.
what_each_reports.P-194: Early MCI vs late MCI (273 E-MCI vs 187 L-MCI, with 211 NC and 160 AD as auxiliary source domain; ADNI VBM-MRI and FDG-PET ROI features). Best 10-fold CV accuracy 68.76 +/- 7.53% (FDG, rMLTFL, Sinkhorn OT), AUC 0.66; bootstrap-aggregated test accuracy up to 75.00% (FDG, SD L1l2/linear), AUC up to 0.79; VBM-only accuracies 57.86-68.48%. No figure of 53% appears in the paper.

quantity_a: Discrimination accuracy of cognitively normal vs MCI, single-split held-out test (n~28 test subjects), amygdala shape/volume features from sMRI
quantity_b: Discrimination accuracy of early MCI vs late MCI (MCI sub-staging, no normal controls in the target task), 10-fold CV and 80/20 bagged test, VBM-MRI and FDG-PET ROI features with AD/NC transfer
incompatible_if_same: No even then: two different feature sets and models each reporting their own accuracy, and neither paper claims an ordering that the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: P-125 is NC vs MCI detection; P-194 is E-MCI vs L-MCI stratification (the record's shared 'T1' label hides two different classification problems)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (different subject subsets and phases)
gates.modality_family: partial mismatch: P-125 structural MRI only; P-194's headline results are FDG-PET (best) and VBM-MRI, with combined FDG+VBM also reported

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (accuracy) but on different class contrasts (NC/MCI vs EMCI/LMCI), so the accuracies measure different things
performance_validity: flag does not apply: P-125 reports ~80% accuracy (below 0.97) and P-194 below 0.80; this is a performance comparison but not one resting on a near-ceiling study
independence: Distinct author groups; both draw on ADNI, possibly overlapping subjects, but the class contrasts are different
grounds: P-125 classifies healthy controls against MCI, whereas P-194 classifies early against late MCI, so the two accuracies are for different class contrasts.
P-194's input features and best results are FDG-PET based, while P-125 uses sMRI amygdala shape features only.
The record's 'Acc 53' for P-194 is not in the paper; its reported accuracies range 56.79-75.00%, so even the stated gap is misrecorded.
The existing partially_resolved status relies on a list of intermediate scores, which is not a condition separating the two results; the correct reason is that the quantities differ.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-194: Acc 53 on T1' is not supported: no 53% accuracy appears in P-194; reported accuracies are 56.79-75.00% (lowest baseline SVM 57.61%).
task_equal 'Yes' is wrong: P-125 is NC vs MCI, P-194 is E-MCI vs L-MCI.
Registry Sample_N_Approx 202 for P-194 is the ADNI-1 subject count quoted in the text; the analysed sample is 831 (211 NC, 273 E-MCI, 187 L-MCI, 160 AD), 460 in the target task.
Registry Modality 'MRI/PET' for P-125 is wrong: P-125 uses T1 MRI only.
gap_magnitude 0.291 is computed from the unsupported 53% figure.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only a P-194 result on NC vs MCI (it reports such an experiment only in a supplementary table not in the extract) compared with P-125 under the same contrast; even then, two different feature sets with overlapping-range accuracies would not be incompatible.
